questions.prompt: What element marks where projected content should render inside a component?
questions.explanation: <ng-content> is the compile-time placeholder for projected content (Angular's equivalent of the native <slot>).

questions.prompt: Against which component's class do bindings inside projected content resolve?

options.text: The parent component that supplies the content
Whichever is closest in the DOM

questions.explanation: Projected content is compiled against the parent's class even though it renders inside the child's DOM.

questions.prompt: With multiple select-based slots and no catch-all, what happens to an element that matches no selector?

options.text: It renders in the first slot
It is silently dropped and not rendered
It renders after the last slot

questions.explanation: Without a plain <ng-content> catch-all, unmatched elements silently disappear from the DOM.

options.text: To alias an element's selector identity so it matches a slot (e.g. when wrapped in <ng-container>)

questions.explanation: ngProjectAs takes a static string and tells Angular to treat the element as if it matched that selector.

questions.prompt: Which is the modern, signal-based way to query projected content (stable since v19)?
questions.explanation: contentChild()/contentChildren() return signals; view queries (viewChild) only see the component's own template.

questions.prompt: Why shouldn't you wrap <ng-content> in @if inside the child's own template?

options.text: Angular still creates the projected DOM nodes regardless, so it doesn't give true conditional rendering — use [hidden] or omit the slot instead
@if cannot be used in child components

questions.explanation: Conditionally wrapping <ng-content> doesn't lazily create content; prefer a CSS toggle like [hidden] or fallback content.
